item: A DuckDB FATAL error at serve time drops the unusable rollup; the memory wall keeps the duckdb-limit stop at stage serve-fatal (inferred, R160 rules)
summary: A served query that hits DuckDB's FatalException leaves the instance unusable, but the serve swallowed every query error and kept the connection, so each later query would fail and fall back. columnar now leaves the kind of fatal (allocation, by class name plus the one fixed phrase, or other) for rollup_serve to take, keyed to the connection; rollup_serve drops the connection, answers live, and for the memory wall keeps the same duckdb-limit stop a build gets at stage serve-fatal (released by the existing rules); any other fatal is a plain failure, dropped and counted. The serve check treats a fatal the same way (the wall is a stop; any other fatal means the instance is not served). No engine text is kept. INFERRED: a serve-time fatal has not been observed; the tests stand in for it.
